findings.input: single C cell, 70 turns, ttft_ms=100+10i so r_lag1=0.9571, n_eff=1.53
findings.why: effective_n_verdict() sets the grid verdict to not_adjudicable_effective_n only after arm_stats() has already emitted p50/p95; the renderer prints the arm table including p95 for the binding arm. The card requires no interval when n_eff<60.

findings.detail: with negative lag-1 r the n_eff formula inflates above n_used; at n_used=59 it reached 2287.74, so the grid became adjudicable while p95 was REFUSED and n_used was below the 60 floor. No unlicensed p95 number was printed, so not counted as an unsound case, but it means the effective-n floor can be passed by anti-correlation.

absent_usable_for: refused by name: cell_inclusion() sees usable_for None and returns refused_usable_for_absent; the 70 abandoned rows were dropped before provenance/pooling and H1 n_raw stayed 70. The analyser's own include-on-absence (analyze_stats.py:749) is neutralised at the consumer.
can_trust_with_16_cells: no — H2 and TVS are pooled across incomparable provenance, and the effective-n refusal is announced while its interval is still printed.
